results.statement: For factorized bilinear maps with local exchange parities epsilon_i, the composite exchange parity is the product of epsilon_i.
A nonzero bipartite alternating composition law can be obtained as B_A tensor B_B from alternating local closures alone.
results.smallest_decisive_counterexample: n=2 with B(x,y)=(x0*y1-x1*y0)e0 and z=e0 tensor e0 + e1 tensor e1; (B tensor B)(z,z)=2 e0 tensor e0 != 0

results.statement: A parity-correct nonzero factorized alternating composite can be formed from one alternating and one symmetric local factor, e.g. B tensor S + S tensor B.
The need for paired skew/symmetric products in composability is historically novel to PDT.
prior_art: Grgin & Petersen, Commun. Math. Phys. 50 (1976) 177-188, DOI 10.1007/BF01617995

results.statement: PDT derives an independently motivated symmetric companion from its existing primitives, rather than importing the quantum Jordan product.
A genuinely PDT-native nonfactorized composition law survives locality, associativity/grouping, quotient, resource, and same-input tests.

dimension_audit: n=1..12,16,24,32,48,64,96,128; n=1 degenerate, decisive B tensor B witness in every tested n>=2
multipartite_audit: B^{tensor N} exchange parity checked analytically and frozen for N=1..12: alternating for odd N, symmetric for even N
